title: Thermo-X-rays Diffraction Analysis of Carbides Crystallization in CrMnFeCoNi, CrMnFeCoNiV0.5 and CrMnFeCoNiMo0.5 High Entropy Alloys
content: In recent years, a new group of alloys has emerged known as High Entropy Alloys (HEA) [1]. These alloys exhibit excellent mechanical and functional properties [2]. Therefore, the analysis and investigation of methods for the large-scale production of HEA is essential. High-energy ball milling (HEBM) is the most effective method [3]. However, carbon-rich process control agents (PCA) are commonly used, such as stearic acid, isopropyl alcohol, ethanol, n-heptane and toluene, to prevent aggregation and stabilize the separated particles [4]. Carbon is trapped in HEA's interstices and structural defects during milling, forming carbide precipitates (MxCy) through heat treatment. [5]. Carbide formation in the HEA matrix improves its structural properties for applications in severe conditions, as in Fe3C-reinforced steels or WC cermet [6]. Therefore, in this study, the crystallization process of carbides is evaluated by the effects of the process control agent in the CrMnFeCoNi, CrMnFeCoNiV0.5 and CrMnFeCoNiMo0.5 HEAs.
